reason: The paper rider is the only available action and should help answer Jo’s question about how the cord moves.
expectation: I expect the rider to show whether a point on the cord travels along with the wiggle, though I’m not sure exactly how it will move.

effect: The rider shows that the disturbance travels while the cord at that point stays roughly in place.
reaction: That is a satisfying, clear demonstration of the difference.
reason: The tension-adjusting key is the only offered combination and may change how the wave behaves.
expectation: I expect adjusting the tension to change the cord's motion, though I don't know exactly how.

effect: Adjusting tension and speed produced a repeating two-loop pattern with a nearly still point.
reaction: The stationary loops are an interesting contrast to the travelling wiggle.
reason: The soundbox is the only offered combination and seems relevant to playing the cord as a string.
expectation: I expect the hollow box to help make the cord's vibrations audible, though I don't know how it will be fitted.

effect: The soundbox is fitted, but its effect on the sound has not yet been demonstrated.
reason: The bridge is the only offered combination and should help prepare the cord for playing.
expectation: I expect the bridge to support the string and perhaps allow its vibrating length to be adjusted.

effect: The bridge changes the vibrating length and transfers vibration to the soundbox.
reaction: That makes its role clearer and links the wave pattern to the soundbox.
reason: The foot pads are the only offered combination; they may stabilize or cushion the machine.
expectation: I expect the pads to go under the machine, though I’m unsure whether they affect its sound.

effect: The soft feet reduce table buzz, and the motor is now off for playing the cord.
reaction: It was useful to see the pads reduce unwanted vibration without stopping the cord.
reason: The plectrum is the only offered combination and should let me play the cord.
expectation: I expect plucking the cord to produce a sound through the soundbox, though I don't know what it will sound like.

effect: Plucking confirmed that the soundbox makes the twang easier to hear and that shortening the vibrating length raises the note; the machine can also return to making visible loops.
reaction: The two-note tune is a satisfying payoff that connects the wave demonstration to an instrument.

mostWorthwhile.text: Plucking the cord and moving the bridge was most worthwhile: it made the effect of vibrating length audible as well as visible.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the soundbox was the least engaging moment on its own, because its effect was not demonstrated until later.

surprise.text: The rider bobbing in place while the disturbance travelled made the distinction between the wave and the cord especially clear.

arbitrary.text: None felt purposeless, although the foot pads' role was unclear when I chose them; the result explained it.

continue.text: Yes. The chapter connected visible waves to sound through clear experiments, and I would be curious to see another mechanism explored that way, though the single available combination at each step left little choice.
